locations.title: Start here
locations.summary: Play this first: how Trip Tours works.

locations.title: London: the big picture
locations.summary: Two thousand years of London in a few minutes, and what we will be getting up to.

locations.title: Tower of London
locations.summary: Nine hundred years of palace, fortress, zoo and prison beside the Thames.

spot.name: Tower Wharf, below the White Tower
spot.text: Stand on Tower Wharf, the riverside walk outside the Tower's walls, before you go in. Face north, away from the river: the big square White Tower with four corner turrets rises behind the outer wall.

locations.title: Tower Bridge
locations.summary: The Victorian lifting bridge everyone mistakes for London Bridge.

spot.name: North bank path, west of Tower Bridge
spot.text: Stand on the riverside path on the north bank, just west of Tower Bridge, near the Tower of London. Face the bridge side-on so you can see both towers and the high walkways.

locations.title: Somerset House
locations.summary: A Georgian palace of offices, with an ice rink in winter.

spot.name: Somerset House courtyard
spot.text: Stand in the middle of the Somerset House courtyard, through the arch from the Strand. The buildings surround you on all sides; the rink fills the courtyard in winter.

locations.title: Buckingham Palace
locations.summary: The King's London home, with the most famous balcony in the world.

spot.name: Victoria Memorial, facing the Palace
spot.text: Roughly by the Victoria Memorial, the big white statue with the gold winged figure in front of the palace. Stand on its palace side and face the long grey front with the balcony.

locations.title: Parliament Square
locations.summary: Big Ben, the Houses of Parliament and Britain's statues of freedom.

spot.name: Parliament Square, by the Churchill statue
spot.text: Stand on the Parliament Square green, near the big statue of Churchill in his greatcoat. Face east, the way he is looking, towards the clock tower and the Houses of Parliament.

locations.title: Westminster Abbey
locations.summary: Every coronation since ten sixty-six, and the resting place of kings, poets and scientists.

spot.name: Broad Sanctuary, facing the Abbey's west front
spot.text: Stand on the wide pavement of Broad Sanctuary, in front of Westminster Abbey. Step back far enough to see both square towers and the great west door between them.

locations.title: Downing Street
locations.summary: The most famous front door in Britain, behind a set of black gates.

spot.name: Whitehall, opposite the gates of Downing Street
spot.text: Stand on the Whitehall pavement opposite the black gates of Downing Street. Look through the gates down the narrow street: Number 10 is the black door on the right.

locations.title: Churchill War Rooms
locations.summary: The secret bunker under Whitehall where Britain's war was run.

spot.name: King Charles Street, by the War Rooms
spot.text: Stand on King Charles Street near the Clive Steps, the stone steps under the statue of Clive at the park end of the street. The War Rooms entrance is at the bottom of the steps.

locations.title: Piccadilly Circus
locations.summary: London's famous junction of lights, and a statue that isn't who you think.

spot.name: Piccadilly Circus, by the Shaftesbury Memorial fountain
spot.text: Stand near the fountain with the winged archer on top, at Piccadilly Circus. Face the curved wall of giant lit screens.

locations.title: Trafalgar Square
locations.summary: Nelson's Column, four bronze lions, and a Christmas tree from Norway.

spot.name: Trafalgar Square, between the fountains and the National Gallery
spot.text: Stand in Trafalgar Square between the fountains, with the National Gallery's columns behind you. Nelson's Column and the Christmas tree are in front of you.

locations.title: British Museum
locations.summary: The world's first national public museum, home of the Rosetta Stone.

spot.name: British Museum forecourt
spot.text: Stand in the forecourt in front of the British Museum, inside the railings. Face the big columns and the triangle of sculpture on top.

locations.title: Natural History Museum
locations.summary: A cathedral to nature, with a blue whale hanging in the hall.

spot.name: Cromwell Road, facing the Natural History Museum
spot.text: Stand on the Cromwell Road side, in front of the Natural History Museum. Face the long cathedral-like front with its two towers and arched entrance.

locations.title: Hyde Park
locations.summary: Henry the Eighth's hunting ground, now home to Winter Wonderland.

spot.name: Hyde Park Corner, Queen Elizabeth Gate
spot.text: Roughly at Hyde Park Corner, by the Queen Elizabeth Gate. Winter Wonderland is just inside the park: follow the crowds and the lights. The real entrance can move each year.

locations.title: Abbey Road
locations.summary: The most famous zebra crossing in the world.

spot.name: Abbey Road, beside the crossing
spot.text: Roughly beside the zebra crossing on Abbey Road, on the footpath, near the white studio building. Stay on the footpath while you listen; cross only when it is safe.

locations.title: Berlin: the big picture
locations.summary: Kings, emperors, a dictatorship, a wall, and a city that put itself back together.

locations.title: Alexanderplatz and the TV Tower
locations.summary: East Berlin's showpiece square, under the tallest structure in Germany.

spot.name: Alexanderplatz, by the World Clock
spot.text: Stand by the World Clock in Alexanderplatz, the round clock with planets on top. Look up and slightly west: the TV Tower's needle and silver ball are hard to miss.

locations.title: The view from the top
locations.summary: Arnold on the observation deck: what you are looking at in every direction.

spot.text: Go up to the observation deck. Find the big green dome of Berlin Cathedral: that is roughly west. Face it: north is on your right, south on your left, east behind you. Pick the window for the direction you want.

locations.title: The Stasi
locations.summary: East Germany's secret police, and the prison that did not appear on any map.

locations.title: Reichstag
locations.summary: Germany's parliament: fire, war, a divided city, and a glass dome.

spot.name: Platz der Republik, west of the Reichstag
spot.text: Stand on the lawn west of the Reichstag, near the West Portal where the tour meets. Face the columns and the words Dem Deutschen Volke above them.

locations.title: Brandenburg Gate
locations.summary: Berlin's great gate: a stolen statue, a wall, and the night it reopened.

spot.name: Pariser Platz, facing the Brandenburg Gate
spot.text: Stand in Pariser Platz, the square on the east side of the Brandenburg Gate. Face the gate and the four horses on top.

locations.title: Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe
locations.summary: A field of grey concrete blocks remembering six million people.

spot.name: North-west corner of the Memorial field
spot.text: Stand at the north-west corner of the field of grey concrete blocks, near the Brandenburg Gate end. Listen here, at the edge, before you walk in.

locations.title: Führerbunker site
locations.summary: An ordinary car park above the place where Hitler's regime ended.

spot.name: Gertrud-Kolmar-Straße, by the information board
spot.text: Roughly on Gertrud-Kolmar-Strasse, near the information board about the bunker. There is nothing to see above ground but a car park; the board marks the place.

locations.title: Topography of Terror
locations.summary: The site of the Gestapo and SS headquarters, beside a surviving stretch of the Wall.

spot.name: Topography of Terror outdoor trench, beside the Wall
spot.text: Roughly at the Topography of Terror outdoor exhibition, beside the surviving stretch of the Wall and the trench below it. Find the long section of grey Wall.

locations.title: Checkpoint Charlie
locations.summary: The most famous crossing point between East and West Berlin.

spot.name: Pavement beside the Checkpoint Charlie guardhouse
spot.text: Stand on the pavement beside the guardhouse replica in the middle of Friedrichstrasse, near the big sign about leaving the American sector.

locations.title: Leipziger Platz and the Spy Museum
locations.summary: Once Europe's busiest square, then a death strip, then a spy museum.

spot.name: Leipziger Platz, facing the Spy Museum
spot.text: Stand in Leipziger Platz, the octagon-shaped square next to Potsdamer Platz. The Spy Museum is on the square's south side.

locations.title: Bernauer Strasse
locations.summary: The Berlin Wall Memorial, with the last preserved stretch of the death strip.

spot.name: Bernauer Straße, Documentation Centre
spot.text: Roughly at the Documentation Centre on Bernauer Strasse, across from the preserved strip of the Wall. If you go up the viewing tower, look down into the death strip.

locations.title: Window of Remembrance
locations.summary: Portraits of those who died at the Wall, and a chapel where a church once stood.

spot.name: Bernauer Straße, Window of Remembrance
spot.text: Roughly on Bernauer Strasse near the Chapel of Reconciliation, the round building, and the Window of Remembrance, the wall of small photographs.

locations.title: Nordbahnhof ghost station
locations.summary: An underground station where trains passed through without stopping.

spot.name: Nordbahnhof station
spot.text: Roughly at Nordbahnhof station. The exhibition about the ghost stations is inside the station hall, down the steps. Phone location may be poor here.

locations.title: Bebelplatz
locations.summary: The square where the Nazis burned books in nineteen thirty-three.

spot.name: Bebelplatz, glass panel
spot.text: Stand in the middle of Bebelplatz, by the glass panel set into the ground. Look down through the glass at the empty white bookshelves below.

locations.title: Train to Dresden
locations.summary: Two hours south through the old East Germany to the capital of Saxony.

locations.title: Striezelmarkt
locations.summary: One of Germany's oldest Christmas markets, home of the Dresden Stollen.

spot.name: Altmarkt, Striezelmarkt
spot.text: Stand in the Altmarkt, the big square where the Striezelmarkt is held. Look for the tall wooden Christmas pyramid.

locations.title: Frauenkirche
locations.summary: The great domed church destroyed in nineteen forty-five and rebuilt from its own ruins.

spot.name: Neumarkt, north-west of the Frauenkirche
spot.text: Stand on Neumarkt, the square north-west of the Frauenkirche, near the statue of Martin Luther. Face the great stone dome.

locations.title: Fürstenzug
locations.summary: A hundred metres of Saxon rulers on porcelain tiles that survived the war.

spot.name: Augustusstraße, across from the Fürstenzug
spot.text: Stand across Augustusstrasse from the long painted tile wall of the Procession of Princes. Face the wall and walk along it.

locations.title: Brühl's Terrace
locations.summary: The Balcony of Europe, high above the river Elbe.

spot.name: Brühl's Terrace
spot.text: Stand on the top of Brühl's Terrace, the raised promenade above the river Elbe. Face the river.

locations.title: Train to Prague
locations.summary: Along the Elbe, through sandstone mountains, into Bohemia.

locations.title: Prague: the big picture
locations.summary: A fairy-tale city that survived the twentieth century almost intact.

locations.title: Prague Castle: First Courtyard
locations.summary: A thousand years of kings, emperors and presidents on one hilltop.

spot.name: Prague Castle, First Courtyard
spot.text: Roughly in the First Courtyard of Prague Castle, just inside the main gate from Hradčany Square, where the guards stand. The Matthias Gate is at the far end.

locations.title: Saint Vitus Cathedral
locations.summary: The Gothic cathedral that took six hundred years to finish.

spot.name: Third Courtyard, facing St Vitus Cathedral
spot.text: Stand in the Third Courtyard, in front of the west end of St Vitus Cathedral. Step back to see both spires.

locations.title: Golden Lane
locations.summary: A lane of tiny painted houses built into the castle wall.

spot.name: Golden Lane
spot.text: Roughly in Golden Lane, the row of tiny painted houses inside the castle grounds. It is part of the paid castle circuit. Find number 22, the blue house.

locations.title: Nerudova Street
locations.summary: A steep street of palaces and painted house signs, on the old royal route.

spot.name: Nerudova Street
spot.text: Stand anywhere along Nerudova Street, the steep street leading up to the castle. Look up above the doorways for the house signs.

locations.title: Old Town Hall and the Astronomical Clock
locations.summary: The six-hundred-year-old Astronomical Clock, and the square where Prague's history played out.

spot.name: Old Town Square, facing the Orloj
spot.text: Stand in Old Town Square facing the south wall of the Old Town Hall tower, where the Astronomical Clock is. Look up at the two clock faces.

locations.title: Old Town Hall Tower
locations.summary: The viewing platform of the Old Town Hall Tower, forty metres above the square, with Sir David watching Prague.

spot.text: Go up the Old Town Hall Tower to the viewing platform. Face the two big dark spires of Týn Church: that is east. The river and Prague Castle are behind you, to the west. Pick the track for the direction you are facing.

locations.title: Charles Bridge
locations.summary: Prague's medieval stone bridge, lined with saints and lit by gas lamps.

spot.name: Křižovnické náměstí, by the Charles IV statue
spot.text: Stand near the Charles IV statue in the small square at the Old Town end of Charles Bridge. Face the tall Gothic tower at the start of the bridge.

locations.title: Old Town Square and Týn Church
locations.summary: Prague's great square, with the twin black spires of Týn Church and the Christmas tree.

spot.name: Old Town Square, by the Jan Hus Memorial
spot.text: Stand near the Jan Hus Memorial in Old Town Square. Face the two black spires of the Týn Church; the Christmas tree is nearby.

locations.title: Josefov, the Jewish Quarter
locations.summary: Prague's old Jewish town: Europe's oldest active synagogue, an ancient cemetery, and the legend of the Golem.

spot.name: Široká street, by the Old-New Synagogue
spot.text: Stand on the street beside the Old-New Synagogue, the small Gothic building with the tall saw-toothed brick gable.

locations.title: Municipal House
locations.summary: Prague's Art Nouveau palace, where Czechoslovakia was born.

spot.name: Republic Square, facing the Municipal House
spot.text: Stand in Republic Square, in front of the Municipal House. Face the big curved mosaic above the entrance.

locations.title: Petřín Lookout Tower
locations.summary: Prague's little Eiffel Tower, on a hill above the city.

spot.name: Petřín Lookout Tower, base
spot.text: Roughly at the base of the Petřín Lookout Tower, the small Eiffel Tower on top of Petřín Hill. You cannot miss it.

locations.title: Saint Nicholas Church, Lesser Town
locations.summary: Prague's great Baroque church, with a dome, a concert and a spy's lookout.

spot.name: Malostranské náměstí, facing St Nicholas
spot.text: Stand in Malostranské náměstí, the Lesser Town Square, beside St Nicholas Church. Face the great green dome and the bell tower.

locations.title: Night train to Kraków
locations.summary: Overnight from Prague across the border into Poland.

locations.title: Kraków: the big picture
locations.summary: Poland's royal city: kings, a dragon, and the darkest chapter of the war.

locations.title: Kraków Market Square
locations.summary: Europe's largest medieval market square, with a trumpet call that stops mid-note.

spot.name: Market Square, beside the Cloth Hall
spot.text: Stand beside the Cloth Hall, the long building in the middle of the Main Market Square. Face St Mary's Basilica, the brick church with two different towers.

locations.title: Schindler's Factory
locations.summary: The enamel factory where Oskar Schindler protected his Jewish workers.

spot.name: Schindler's Factory gate
spot.text: Roughly at the gate of Schindler's Factory, the museum on Lipowa Street. Look for the factory front and the entrance gate.

locations.title: Ghetto Heroes Square
locations.summary: The square of empty chairs, at the heart of the wartime Jewish ghetto.

spot.name: Ghetto Heroes Square, Chairs Memorial
spot.text: Stand in Ghetto Heroes Square, among the large metal chairs that fill the square.

locations.title: Eagle Pharmacy
locations.summary: The pharmacy whose owner stayed inside the ghetto to help.

spot.name: Ghetto Heroes Square, opposite the Eagle Pharmacy
spot.text: Stand in Ghetto Heroes Square, facing the corner building that houses the Eagle Pharmacy museum.

locations.title: Ghetto wall fragment
locations.summary: A surviving piece of the wall that enclosed the Kraków ghetto.

spot.name: ul. Lwowska, ghetto wall fragment
spot.text: Roughly on Lwowska Street, by the surviving piece of the ghetto wall with the rounded tops and the plaque.

locations.title: Ride to Auschwitz-Birkenau
locations.summary: The journey west from Kraków to the former German death camp.

locations.title: Wawel Hill
locations.summary: The royal castle and cathedral of Poland's kings, and the lair of a dragon.

spot.name: Foot of Wawel Hill
spot.text: Roughly at the foot of Wawel Hill, near the path that leads up to the castle gate. Look up at the castle walls on the hill.

locations.title: Wawel Dragon statue
locations.summary: A bronze dragon by the river that breathes real fire.

spot.name: Wawel Dragon statue
spot.text: Stand on the riverside below Wawel Hill, near the bronze dragon by the cave entrance. Wait a few minutes for the fire.

locations.title: Night train to Budapest
locations.summary: Overnight from Kraków, across Slovakia, to Budapest.

locations.title: Budapest: the big picture
locations.summary: Two cities on the Danube, hot springs underneath, and a revolution against tanks.

locations.title: Chain Bridge
locations.summary: The first permanent bridge between Buda and Pest, guarded by stone lions.

spot.name: Széchenyi István tér, Pest bridgehead
spot.text: Stand in Széchenyi István tér, the square at the Pest end of the Chain Bridge. Face the bridge and the stone lions.

locations.title: Fisherman's Bastion
locations.summary: A fairy-tale terrace of white towers with the best view of Parliament.

spot.name: Fisherman's Bastion
spot.text: Roughly on the terraces of Fisherman's Bastion, the white towers beside Matthias Church on Castle Hill. Look east across the Danube: the Parliament is the huge building on the far bank.

locations.title: The Danube
locations.summary: Europe's great river, flowing through ten countries and four capital cities.

spot.name: Vigadó tér, Dock 7
spot.text: Roughly at the riverside on the Pest side near Vigadó tér, where the cruise boats moor. Check the booking for the pier: Dock 7.

locations.title: Hungarian Parliament
locations.summary: Hungary's enormous Gothic parliament, home of the Holy Crown.

spot.name: Kossuth Lajos tér, facing Parliament
spot.text: Stand in Kossuth Lajos tér, the big square in front of the Parliament. Face the building and its dome.

locations.title: Shoes on the Danube Bank
locations.summary: Sixty pairs of iron shoes on the riverbank, remembering those murdered here.

spot.name: Shoes on the Danube Bank
spot.text: Roughly on the riverside promenade south of the Parliament, at the iron shoes along the water's edge. Stand back from the edge. This is a memorial.

locations.title: Batthyány tér
locations.summary: The postcard view of Parliament from the Buda bank.

spot.name: Buda embankment, Batthyány tér
spot.text: Roughly on the Buda embankment by Batthyány tér, facing across the Danube. The Parliament stretches along the opposite bank.

locations.title: Vajdahunyad Castle and City Park
locations.summary: A castle built for a party, beside one of Europe's oldest ice rinks.

spot.name: City Park lake, facing Vajdahunyad Castle
spot.text: Roughly by the lake in City Park, facing Vajdahunyad Castle, the castle of many styles. In winter the lake is the ice rink.

locations.title: Heroes' Square
locations.summary: Hungary's great monument to a thousand years of history.

spot.name: Heroes' Square
spot.text: Stand in Heroes' Square, in front of the tall column with the angel on top and the seven horsemen at its base.

locations.title: Széchenyi Baths
locations.summary: One of Europe's largest thermal baths, open to the sky in winter.

spot.name: Széchenyi Baths, outside the yellow façade
spot.text: Roughly outside the big yellow building of the Széchenyi Baths in City Park.

locations.title: Egypt: the big picture
locations.summary: Five thousand years of pharaohs, pyramids and the river that made it all possible.

locations.title: Saqqara and Dahshur
locations.summary: The first pyramid ever built, and the pyramids where the builders learned their craft.

locations.title: Giza Pyramids and Khan el-Khalili
locations.summary: The Great Pyramid, the Sphinx, and Cairo's great bazaar.

locations.title: Grand Egyptian Museum and the royal mummies
locations.summary: The world's biggest museum of a single civilisation, and the hall of the royal mummies.

locations.title: Aswan and Nubia
locations.summary: Egypt's southern frontier, granite quarries, and the land of the Nubians.

locations.title: Abu Simbel
locations.summary: Ramesses the Second's colossal temples, cut out of a mountain and moved to save them.

locations.title: Philae and the Unfinished Obelisk
locations.summary: The island temple of Isis, the last of the old religion, and the obelisk that cracked.

locations.title: Kom Ombo and Edfu
locations.summary: A temple for two gods, and the best-preserved temple in Egypt.

locations.title: Sailing the Nile
locations.summary: Life on the banks from the deck: Aswan's islands, the river's gift, the lock at Esna, and the arrival at Luxor.

spot.text: On the sun deck or at a window of the ship, with the river bank in view. No spot needed: play these as the ship sails north from Aswan to Luxor, and pick the track that matches what you can see.

locations.title: Karnak and Luxor Temple
locations.summary: The greatest temple complex ever built, and the temple at the heart of Luxor.

locations.title: Valley of the Kings
locations.summary: The hidden royal tombs of the West Bank, the woman pharaoh, and the singing statue.

locations.title: Valley of the Queens and the workers' village
locations.summary: Nefertari's painted tomb, the village of the tomb builders, and Ramesses' fallen giant.

locations.title: Istanbul: the big picture
locations.summary: One city, two continents, three empires.

locations.title: Süleymaniye Mosque
locations.summary: The great mosque of Süleyman the Magnificent, by the architect Sinan, above the Golden Horn.

spot.name: Süleymaniye Mosque terrace
spot.text: Roughly on the terrace of the Süleymaniye Mosque, on the Golden Horn side of the grounds. Look out over the water.

locations.title: Hagia Sophia
locations.summary: Fifteen hundred years as a church, a mosque, a museum, and a mosque again.

spot.name: Sultanahmet Park, facing Hagia Sophia
spot.text: Stand in Sultanahmet Park, the gardens between Hagia Sophia and the Blue Mosque. Face Hagia Sophia, the huge dome with four minarets.

locations.title: Topkapı Palace
locations.summary: The palace of the Ottoman sultans for four hundred years.

spot.name: Outside the Imperial Gate
spot.text: Roughly in the square in front of the Imperial Gate of Topkapı Palace, near the ornate fountain, behind Hagia Sophia.

locations.title: Basilica Cistern
locations.summary: A vast underground Roman water reservoir, with upside-down Medusa heads.

spot.name: Basilica Cistern entrance
spot.text: Roughly at the entrance building of the Basilica Cistern, near Hagia Sophia. Phone location may be poor once you go underground.

locations.title: Grand Bazaar
locations.summary: One of the oldest and largest covered markets in the world.

spot.name: Grand Bazaar, Nuruosmaniye gate
spot.text: Roughly near the Nuruosmaniye gate of the Grand Bazaar, beside the Nuruosmaniye Mosque. Look for the big arched gateway into the bazaar.

locations.title: Gallipoli: the ride out
locations.summary: The long road to the Gallipoli peninsula, where Australians, New Zealanders, Turks and others fought in nineteen fifteen.

locations.title: Gallipoli: the ride home
locations.summary: A quiet reflection on the long road back to Istanbul.

locations.title: The Blue Mosque
locations.summary: Sultan Ahmed's great mosque, with its six minarets and twenty thousand tiles.

spot.name: Hippodrome, looking at the Blue Mosque
spot.text: Stand in the Hippodrome near the ancient obelisks. Face the Blue Mosque with its cascade of domes and six minarets.

locations.title: Hippodrome and the Egyptian Obelisk
locations.summary: The old chariot-racing track of Constantinople, with an obelisk from Karnak.

spot.name: Hippodrome, by the Obelisk of Theodosius
spot.text: Roughly beside the Obelisk of Theodosius, the carved Egyptian obelisk in the Hippodrome, with its picture-covered marble base.

sessions.title: Start here
sessions.summary: How this works, why there will be a test, and why everything that goes wrong is somebody else's fault.
sessions.listenAt: First. On the flight, or any time before London.

sessions.title: London: the big picture
sessions.summary: Sir David on how London grew, from a Roman bridge to a global city, the war that nearly destroyed it, and what the next four days hold.
sessions.listenAt: On the flight, or on arrival in London.

sessions.title: The fortress by the river
sessions.summary: Sir David observes the White Tower, the royal zoo and the ravens, then hands you to the Tower's own guide.
sessions.listenAt: Tower Wharf, by the river wall just west of the White Tower

sessions.title: The bridge that lifts
sessions.summary: How Tower Bridge works, why it is dressed up as a castle, and the bus that jumped it.
sessions.listenAt: North bank riverside path, just west of the north tower

sessions.title: Skating in a palace courtyard
sessions.summary: The palace that became government offices, and the river that used to reach its doors.
sessions.listenAt: Under the Strand arch, courtyard centre before skating (16:00)

sessions.title: The palace and the guards
sessions.summary: Whose house it was first, how to tell if the King is home, and how to tell the guards apart.
sessions.listenAt: Victoria Memorial steps, facing the palace front (or on the Mall for the guard approach)

sessions.title: Big Ben, um, sorry
sessions.summary: Hugh tries to talk about the clock tower without saying anything unfortunate, then the statues around the square.
sessions.listenAt: Parliament Square green, near the Churchill statue

sessions.title: The coronation church
sessions.summary: Hugh on the Abbey's front, the modern martyrs above the door, and what to find inside.
sessions.listenAt: Broad Sanctuary, facing the west front

sessions.title: The door at Number Ten
sessions.summary: Hugh on the street, the man it is named after, the door that cannot be opened from outside, and a confession.
sessions.listenAt: On Whitehall, opposite the Downing Street gates.

sessions.title: The bunker under your feet
sessions.summary: Hugh on the secret rooms beneath this street, Churchill's onesie, and Dad's war cabinet.
sessions.listenAt: King Charles Street, outside the entrance

sessions.title: Lights and ruffles
sessions.summary: Sir David returns for the evening lights: a frilly collar, a famous archer, and the screens.
sessions.listenAt: Beside the Eros fountain

sessions.title: Nelson, lions and a Norwegian tree
sessions.summary: Who stands on top of the column, the tree from Oslo, and the true centre of London.
sessions.listenAt: In front of the National Gallery steps

sessions.title: Night at the British Museum
sessions.summary: Two familiar-sounding museum regulars take over: the front of the building, a film connection, and the stone that unlocked ancient Egypt.
sessions.listenAt: Forecourt, facing the Greek Revival portico

sessions.title: The cathedral of nature
sessions.summary: Sir David is finally in his element, and Ben and Owen are not: carved animals, the man who named the dinosaurs, and the whale.
sessions.listenAt: Cromwell Road forecourt, facing the main facade

sessions.title: A king's hunting ground
sessions.summary: How Hyde Park began, the Great Exhibition of eighteen fifty-one, and a word about the weather at home.
sessions.listenAt: At the main entrance near Hyde Park Corner

sessions.title: Four guys, one crossing
sessions.summary: The ten-minute photo shoot that made a road crossing famous, and goodbye to London.
sessions.listenAt: Pavement on the St John's Wood side, off the road

sessions.title: Berlin: the big picture
sessions.summary: Arnold on how Berlin became Germany's capital, Sir Laurence on the twentieth century, and what the next few days hold.
sessions.listenAt: The evening before, or on the flight to Berlin.

sessions.title: Arnold arrives
sessions.summary: Arnold introduces himself, Berlin, the TV Tower, the Pope's revenge, and the kids' new bank cards.
sessions.listenAt: By the World Clock (Weltzeituhr), looking up

sessions.title: Arnold's view from the top
sessions.summary: Find your way round the deck, then north, east, south and west, finishing with the sunset.
sessions.listenAt: Up on the observation deck of the TV Tower, 203 metres above Alexanderplatz.

sessions.title: Before Hohenschönhausen
sessions.summary: A quiet introduction to the Stasi and the prison you are about to visit with a guide.
sessions.listenAt: Tram/bus or on the walk in

sessions.title: The waiting thirty minutes
sessions.summary: Arnold tells the Reichstag's story while you wait for the tour: the inscription, the fire, the flag, the Wall, the wrapping, and the dome.
sessions.listenAt: Platz der Republik lawn, west of the building, facing the West Portal (meet 11:30)

sessions.title: The gate in no-man's land
sessions.summary: The chariot on top, Napoleon's theft, the Wall, and why the twenty-second of December matters here.
sessions.listenAt: Pariser Platz, centre of the square

sessions.title: The field of stones
sessions.summary: What this memorial is, and how to walk through it.
sessions.listenAt: North-west corner of the field, then a few steps in

sessions.title: The end, underground
sessions.summary: Why there is nothing to see here, and why that was deliberate.
sessions.listenAt: At the information board on Gertrud-Kolmar-Strasse
